items.summary: X-rays with wavelengths between approximately 2.3 and 4.4 nanometers, i.e., in the so-called water window, are particularly well suited to examining biological samples in their natural, aqueous environment.

items.title: Temporal Progression of Prior Precision, Surprisal, Model Updating and Tone Adaptation in Human Auditory Cortices
items.summary: Auditory perception emerges from the continuous integration of incoming acoustic signals with statistical predictions, a process complemented by simpler local adaptation. Yet, how all these concurrent mechanisms unfold in time remains underexplored. Using magnetoencephalography (MEG) in participants listening to stochastic tone sequences with periodically shifting inferential statistics, we modelled the temporal, spatial, and spectral dynamics of stimulus-specific repetition suppression, surprisal, model updating, and prior precision. By concurrently tracking these computational parameters within this dynamic auditory environment, we revealed a distinct chronological hierarchy governing predictive and adaptive processing. Prior precision states - reflecting expectations - emerged earliest, followed by rapid and concurrent repetition suppression and surprisal - reflecting local acoustic attenuation and global mismatch detection.
items.author: van Haren, J. J. G., de Lange, F. P., Kotz, S. A. et al.

items.title: Ranging and territoriality in African Apes
items.summary: Intergroup relations vary strikingly among African apes, with only chimpanzees showing intense, often lethal territoriality. The economic defendability hypothesis proposes that such territorial behaviour is favored where home ranges can be economically defended, as indexed by the ratio of daily travel distance to home range diameter. To test this idea, we compiled and analyzed comparable data on yearly home range size, daily travel distance and defendability indices from one population of each nonhuman African ape species and integrated these with comparable published data. We find that bonobos had substantially larger home ranges and longer daily travel distances than chimpanzees and gorillas, contradicting a prevailing assumption that bonobos experience higher or more reliable food abundance.
items.author: Surbeck, M., Supple, R., Massaro, A. P. et al.

items.title: Structural Basis for Human Milk Oligosaccharides Recognition by Evolutionarily Dominant Norovirus Genogroup II Genotypes
items.summary: Human noroviruses are a major cause of acute gastroenteritis. Human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs) contain glycan motifs similar to histo-blood group antigens and may act as soluble decoys that reduce viral attachment. However, the molecular basis of HMO recognition by the P domain of the major capsid protein VP1 of different norovirus genotypes is not fully understood. Here, we combined ligand-based and protein-based NMR experiments with X-ray crystallography to study HMO binding to the P domain of the latent GII.2, dominant GII.4 and emerging GII.17 noroviruses genotypes. Screening of 12 HMOs by STD NMR showed binding of all fucosylated HMOs to GII.4 and GII.17 and none for non-fucosylated HMOs.
items.author: Pisapia, L., Flatau, H. N., Lin, S. et al.

items.title: PREMISE: A Quality-Aware Probabilistic Framework for High-Resolution Source Assignment in Metagenomic Sequencing
items.summary: Metagenomic applications, from influenza A virus (IAV) subtype tracking to bacterial strain resolution, frequently require sub-species resolution.However, traditional $k$-mer-based methods fragment reads into short $k$-mers and discard per-base quality scores.By omitting both intra-read linkage and error information, these methods confound closely related genomic variants, thereby impeding real-time pathogen surveillance and containment.We introduce \premise (Pathogen Resolution via Expectation-Maximization In Sequencing Experiments), a probabilistic, alignment-based framework implemented in Rust for high-resolution source assignment against near-complete reference databases.\premise aligns whole reads using a bidirectional run-length FM-index and quantifies reference abundances with a quality-aware Expectation-Maximization algorithm mapped over a taxonomy.This framework applies an optional sparsity penalty to resolve ambiguous assignments, which is particularly important when sparse samples are mapped against reference databases rich in highly homologous candidate references.On ten dense CAMI II strain-madness samples, \premise achieves the highest species-level read classification F1 score ($0.992$) among eight evaluated methods, with no false-positive or missed species.At…
items.author: Vijendran, S., Dorman, K., Anderson, T. K. et al.

items.title: Mathematical model of phenotypic plasticity predicts interconversion is a drug target for neuroblastoma.
items.summary: Neuroblastoma is a paediatric cancer arising from the sympathetic nervous system as neural crest cells, made up of noradrenergic (NOR/ADRN/N), mesenchymal like (MES/S), and intermediate (I-type/I) cell types. These cells can interconvert between types, contributing to treatment resistance and relapse. We developed a mathematical model to investigate how interconversion patterns affect the efficacy of phenotype-specific inhibitors. We used three ordinary differential equations to describe the dynamics of the three populations, including logistic growth, interconversion, and drug-induced death. Of the 64 possible interconversion patterns, five reduced the target population: two for N cells and three for S cells. N targeting patterns were more effective with higher interconversion rates, while mesenchymal targeting patterns were more effective with lower interconversion rates.
items.author: Covell, F., Patel, M., Wertheim, K. Y.

items.title: Residual Hearing Loss After Chronic Cochlear Implantation in Guinea Pigs is Primarily Conductive
items.summary: It is desirous to preserve residual low-frequency hearing in cochlear implant recipients, as dual stimulation using electrical and acoustic signals results in superior speech-in-noise processing and musicality. However, cochlear implant recipients commonly lose their residual acoustic hearing gradually following surgical placement of the array. The governing mechanism is not understood and is likely due to multiple factors including surgical trauma, inflammation, and the foreign body induced immune response to the array, including formation of intracochlear fibrosis. Normal mechanical function of the cochlea is expected to underpin residual hearing but has not been directly studied. This function includes efficient transmission of sound to the cochlea via the middle ear, sound propagation via the basilar membrane travelling wave, mechanical tuning characteristics, and the non-linear cochlear amplification of responses to low-frequency stimulation.
items.author: He, W., Xing, R., Hill, J. D. et al.

items.title: β-cell NCK1 is reduced in type 2 diabetes, impairing the unfolded protein response and insulin secretion while revealing sex-specific adaptation
items.summary: Type 2 diabetes is characterized by failure of pancreatic {beta} cells to adapt insulin secretion to metabolic demand, causing {beta} cell function and reduced {beta} cell mass. The unfolded protein response (UPR) is central to adaptation by maintaining endoplasmic reticulum homeostasis and supporting insulin biosynthesis, secretion, proliferation, and survival. NCK1, is an adaptor protein that regulates insulin biosynthesis and UPR activation, positioning it at the crossroads of several processes essential for {beta} cell function. We found in mouse and human islets that NCK1 expression was upregulated by glucose and reduced in individuals living with type 2 diabetes. We thus explored the importance of {beta} cell NCK1 in endocrine function and glucose homeostasis using INS 1 cells, mouse and human islets, and {beta} cell specific knockout male and female mice (NCK1{beta}KO).
items.author: Monteillet, L., Jouvet, N., Huet, R. et al.

items.title: Secondary growth in the tomato stem is suppressed by the flowering regulators FUL2 and STM3
items.summary: Herbaceous eudicot crops such as tomato accumulate substantial amounts of secondary xylem in their stems, particularly in the basal part. As plants progress from the vegetative phase to flowering and fruit development, secondary growth continues to provide mechanical support and facilitate transport. To uncover how secondary growth is regulated in the tomato stem, we used laser capture microdissection RNA-seq to establish tissue-specific transcriptomic profiles. This revealed that key regulators associated with wood formation in poplar are also acting in tomato. Furthermore, we found that the flowering regulators FUL2 and STM3 are substantially expressed in xylem tissue. Subsequent functional analysis identified FUL2 and STM3 as key repressors of secondary growth, with ful2 or stm3 knock-out mutants exhibiting strongly increased secondary growth in older tomato stems.
items.author: Pandey, K., Appiah, A. P., van Velzen, R. et al.

items.title: A three-factor model can explain symmetry breaking and the n-1 rule during X-chromosome inactivation
items.summary: X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) is a mammalian gene regulatory process that via chromosome-scale transcriptional silencing, leaves active a single X chromosome per diploid genome complement. The mechanisms that enable cells to select the appropriate number of X chromosomes to inactivate while leaving others active remain unclear. We demonstrate that all known chromosomal counting scenarios during XCI can be accounted for by a three-factor mathematical model that includes (1) Xist, the long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) responsible for gene silencing during XCI in eutherians, (2) an X-linked transcriptional activator of Xist, and (3) the autosomally-encoded SPEN, an Xist RNA-binding protein that is essential for gene silencing during XCI.
items.author: Guan, K., Liu, J. M., Calabrese, J. M. et al.

items.title: Auditory Evoked Potentials Differ from Controls and Correlate with Aspects of Cognition in Kabuki Syndrome and Rubinstein-Taybi Syndrome
items.summary: Objective Kabuki syndrome (KS) and Rubinstein-Taybi syndrome (RSTS) are two disorders caused by dysfunctional components of the epigenetic machinery and both result in intellectual disability. Mouse models of both KS and RSTS have seen reversal of cognitive impairment with epigenetic treatments. However, a great need exists for biomarkers in these disorders to improve the likelihood of successful clinical trials. This study aimed to investigate cortical auditory evoked potentials (AEPs) in KS and RSTS so that it could potentially be developed into a response biomarker in the future. Methods The amplitude of the N1-P2-N2 complex was measured for passive listening to monotonal auditory stimuli in individuals with KS, with RSTS, and typically developing controls.
items.author: Kalinousky, A., Bucklin, E., Ng, R. et al.

items.title: Modeling circadian rhythm splitting under chronic light and the asymmetric transition kinetics between lighting conditions
items.summary: In various vertebrates, chronic light splits the single daily 24-h circadian activity bout into two 12-h behavioral components per cycle, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we develop a two-lobe biophysical model of the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) to understand this phenomenon. By representing the master clock as interacting ventral core and dorsal shell populations of Kuramoto-type oscillators across bilateral lobes, we suggest that chronic light changes the excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance orchestrated by GABA, which either inhibits or excites SCN neurons. Under constant darkness, excitation dominates and provides in-phase synchronization of the populations. Under chronic light, inhibition dominates, and the ipsilateral and contralateral couplings among the core and shell populations become negative.
items.author: Goltsev, A. V., Mendes, J. F.

items.title: Robust lesion network mapping reveals symptom-specific circuits
items.summary: Lesion network mapping (LNM) is a powerful tool for linking distributed brain lesions to symptom-relevant networks, but similar LNM maps across unrelated symptoms have raised concerns about its statistical validity and specificity. Here we introduce robust LNM (rLNM), a statistically principled framework that combines two complementary controls: an anatomy-preserving spatial null model to account for connectome-derived hub bias shared across symptoms, and hypothesis-driven contrasts to resolve selective specificity among related symptoms. rLNM effectively controls both false positives and negatives. Across 10 lesion datasets (384 lesions) and two task-fMRI meta-analyses (339 experiments), rLNM recovers distinct symptom-specific networks (mean r = 0.044), which show significantly reduced similarity to the connectome hub pattern (r = 0.12 vs.
items.author: Cui, W., Zhu, J., Long, Y. et al.

items.title: Neural transformation from image realism to perceived realness
items.summary: Humans readily perceive whether a visual stimulus depicts something that could exist in the real world, yet the neural basis of perceived realness remains unclear. Because differences between real and unreal stimuli are ultimately expressed through visual features, realness might be expected to emerge along the ventral visual stream. Contrary to this prediction, we show that perceived-realness representations emerge in higher dorsal visual areas through a transformation of image-realism-related image-feature representations in early visual and early dorsal visual areas. fMRI revealed this representational shift toward intraparietal sulcus (IPS), with IPS patterns predicting perceived realness beyond image features and decision difficulty; source-localized MEG showed that realness coding in IPS emerged later than feature coding in early visual and dorsal visual areas.
items.author: Orima, T., Ban, H.

items.title: A Mathematical Model of Reliability-Dependent Sensory Reweighting in Quiet Standing
items.summary: Human quiet standing relies on vestibular, proprioceptive, and visual information whose contributions change with sensory context. Posturography characterizes this reweighting through responses to visual and support-surface perturbations, but a compact account of how sensory reliability propagates from state estimation to postural action remains incomplete. We develop a minimal quiet-standing model in which sensory reliability is encoded by channel-specific precision parameters that weight sensory prediction errors. A one-link inverted pendulum with intrinsic ankle stiffness estimates posture by minimizing an active-inference free-energy objective and selects ankle torque by minimizing the same objective under a restorative sensory goal. A fixed-point analysis predicts in closed form the perturbation-induced belief bias, each channel's state-update contribution, the steady posture, and a linear stability condition from the precisions, goal dynamics, and intrinsic stiffness.
items.author: Kobayashi, J.

items.title: Emergent topological structure in spontaneous brain-organoid activity
items.summary: Neural activity is widely held to organize on low-dimensional structure embedded in a high-dimensional state space. Persistent homology reads such structure directly from the pattern of pairwise correlations, without assuming in advance which variables are relevant. We apply persistent homology to microelectrode-array (MEA) recordings of spontaneous activity from human (Lancaster) and mouse (Pasca) cortical organoids, spanning 25-197 sorted units, and ask whether topological data analysis resolves structure at the node counts that neural recordings actually deliver. Building weighted networks in correlation space and characterizing them by Vietoris-Rips filtration, we find that the first homology (H1, loops) rises significantly above a rate- and population-preserving null in 14 of 18 datasets, all of which remain significant after correction for testing 18 datasets.
items.author: Bodnia, E., Basart, M., Hai, S. et al.

items.title: γδ T cell-derived IL-17A aggravates experimental epidermolysis bullosa acquisita in response to IL-1β
items.summary: Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita (EBA) is a mucocutaneous autoimmune blistering disorder mediated by autoantibodies against type VII collagen and subsequent splitting of the dermal-epidermal junction. Interleukin (IL)-17A promotes the production of chemokines and cytokines involved in neutrophil recruitment and activation, suggesting that IL-17A may contribute to EBA pathogenesis. We aimed to clarify the role of IL-17A in experimental EBA. Using an antibody transfer-induced EBA mouse model, we demonstrate that IL-17A promotes disease development, as pharmacological blockade of IL-17A with a neutralizing antibody ameliorated skin lesions. Gamma-delta ({gamma}{delta}) T cells were identified as the predominant cellular source of IL-17A, supported by the attenuated disease phenotype observed in {gamma}{delta}TCR-deficient mice.
items.author: Deng, F., Jukic, S., Wannick, M. et al.

items.title: A noncanonical function of Dicer fuels self-dsRNA-driven inflammation
items.summary: Self-derived double-stranded RNA (self-dsRNA) acts as potent triggers of autoinflammation and damage-associated molecular patterns in cancer and infection. However, the upstream processes controlling self-dsRNA homeostasis remain unclear. We uncover a non-canonical role for human Dicer in driving cell-intrinsic immunity to self-dsRNAs that arise from editing or splicing defects, epigenetic deregulation or mitochondrial stress. Dicer loss abolishes type-I interferon induction, PKR activation, and OAS-RNase L activation in response to self - but not exogenous - dsRNA in multiple cell types, including a clinically-relevant hiPSC model of neuroinflammation. Dicer interacts with G3BP1 and LGP2 to regulate self-dsRNA availability and recognition, respectively, independently of miRNAs.
items.author: ter Haar, L. R., de Lange, S., Gravekamp, D. et al.

items.title: Cell-scale confinement reorders bacterial speed rankings
items.summary: Which bacterium swims fastest depends on where the race is run. Speeds are usually measured in open liquid, yet many bacteria live in pores, mucus and host passages no wider than a cell. Using a microfluidic device with eight channel widths (0.80-3.00 m) in one field of view, we tracked unlabeled cells of eight species spanning five motility systems. Chamber height, a polymer additive and channel width each reordered the ranking. Vibrio alginolyticus, the fastest in open liquid, slowed to ~4 m/s in 1.25-m channels, whereas Campylobacter jejuni and Bacillus subtilis kept 33-46 m/s. Open liquid speed did not predict robustness to confinement.
items.author: Shimada, Y. Y., Uemura, N. A., Yoshioka, A. et al.

items.title: Dual regulation of chemical stress-induced DDI2/3 expression by a transcription factor Fzf1 and nucleosome in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
items.summary: DDI2 and DDI3 (DDI2/3) are duplicated genes in Saccharomyces cerevisiae that exhibit strong induction by a transcription factor Fzf1 in response to chemical treatments like cyanamide (CY) and methyl methanesulfonate (MMS). Although, like DDI2/3, SSU1, YHB1 and YNR064C also contain an Fzf1-binding consensus sequence CS2 and are coordinately regulated by Fzf1, these genes are only modestly induced by CY and MMS. To identify additional cis-acting elements in the DDI2/3 promoter, we made DDI2/3 promoter deletions in a reporter system and identified upstream repressing sequences (URS) spanning 480 nucleotides. To test a hypothesis that the chromatin structure constitutes the URS, we utilized a yeast strain capable of histone H3/H4 depletion by shifting carbon sources.
items.author: Du, Y., Lin, A., Brown, J. A. R. et al.

items.title: ER stress-associated IRE1α signalling links impaired QPRT-dependent NAD⁺ biosynthesis to reduced oocyte competence
items.summary: Oocyte quality is closely linked to metabolic and organelle homeostasis, but the mechanisms underlying naturally occurring differences in oocyte quality remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify a link between endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, impaired NAD biosynthesis and poor oocyte quality. Poor-grade goat oocytes exhibited profound NAD depletion, accompanied by quinolinic acid accumulation and reduced expression of quinolinate phosphoribosyltransferase (QPRT), suggesting a bottleneck in de novo NAD biosynthesis. Restoring QPRT expression or bypassing this metabolic step improved meiotic maturation. Further analyses revealed altered ER stress signalling, increased IRE1-associated activity and reduced QPRT RNA stability. Recombinant IRE1 processed QPRT RNA in vitro, suggesting a possible link between IRE1 activity and QPRT transcript regulation.
items.author: Athar, M., E, A. K., Birajdar, P. et al.

items.title: A Dynamic Stem Cell State Links Environmental Cues to Skeletal and Regenerative Fates
items.summary: Stem cells faithfully generate tissue architecture during development, yet how their identity and regenerative output are reshaped as anatomical niches mature and environmental signals change with aging and injury remains poorly understood. Rare skeletal stem cells (SSCs) across diverse skeletal sites are defined by combinations of cell-surface markers, precluding their genetic interrogation in vivo. Here, using spatially informed single cell transcriptomics, we identify Pannexin-3 (Panx3) to mark a dynamic functional state within bona fide SSCs and establish Panx3-CreERT2 mice for its longitudinal interrogation. Panx3 SSCs exhibit long-term clonal persistence, self-renewal and multipotency, whereas Panx3- SSCs can acquire this state. Successive SSC cohorts engage the Panx3 state during skeletal development, osteoanabolic stimulation expands pre-existing Panx3 SSC clones and injury induces it locally in previously unlabeled progenitors.
items.author: Wang, Y., Zhao, L., Chen, K. et al.

items.title: Proteome-wide profiling reveals compartment-specific RNA buffering of protein aggregation during stress
items.summary: Cellular adaptation to stress requires extensive remodeling of RNA metabolism. The rewiring of the RNA-protein interaction landscape and the assembly of biomolecular condensates are central to this response, yet the global stress-induced reorganization of macromolecular RNA-protein assemblies remains incompletely characterized. Here, we apply R-DeeP, a density gradient approach coupled to quantitative mass spectrometry, to profile the RNA-dependent sedimentation behaviour of the Saccha-romyces cerevisiae proteome during heat and salt stress. We demonstrate that stress triggers a profound, stress-specific reorganization of the RNA interactome. Many proteins undergo pronounced, selective shifts into high-molecular weight fractions, indicative of aggregation. RNase treatment markedly exacerbates this aggregation, consistent with the model that RNA acts as a general chaperone that keeps proteins with intrinsically disordered regions soluble.
items.author: Seidler, J. F., Thelen, F., Wäber, N. B. et al.

items.title: Mutually Repressive Transcription Factors Drive Intestinal Maturation for Weaning
items.summary: In mammals, rapid neonatal growth depends on specialized intestinal enterocytes that absorb nutrients from milk. These cells exhibit distinct functions, morphologies, and gene expression programs that support neonatal nutrition before transitioning to an adult state at weaning. However, the transcriptional mechanisms that establish neonatal enterocyte identity and coordinate their maturation remain poorly understood. Here we show that the transcription factors BLIMP1 and CASZ1 form a central switch in the timing of enterocyte maturation. While BLIMP1 marks and promotes neonatal enterocytes, CASZ1 is expressed in adult enterocytes and is required for the proper timing of their emergence. Genetic analysis indicates that these neonatal and adult factors are mutually repressive, forming a genetic switch underlying weaning.
items.author: Scales, M. K., Karsan, R., Underwood, J. et al.

items.title: Body size cascades from Neodiprion sawfly hosts to Perilampid parasitoids: An investigation of sequential divergence
items.summary: Ecological speciation drives diversity in plant-eating insect systems, but it may also generate parallel specialization in parasitoid associates in a cascading effect of "sequential divergence." However, sequential divergence has never been successfully identified in parasitoids of externally feeding insects. To address this gap, we consider the Pinus-Neodiprion-Perilampus neodiprioni system, where plant-associated, externally feeding Neodiprion demonstrate ecological divergence, as supported by body size as a magic trait in sympatric species. It seems possible that this body size differentiation may cascade to Neodiprion's parasitoids via sequential divergence. Therefore, we asked, "Does P. neodiprioni exhibit host-specific divergence in body size that parallels patterns in Neodiprion hosts?" Further, "Does P.
items.author: White, S. V., Mohammed, S., Bagley, R. K.

items.title: Widespread Saccharomyces hybridization in agave fermentations arises repeatedly from asymmetric parental diversity
items.summary: Interspecific hybridization can profoundly reshape genomes by bringing together divergent genetic backgrounds, yet its ecological and evolutionary dynamics remain poorly understood at the population level. Here, we identify an extensive hybridization system in traditional agave fermentations across Mexico involving Saccharomyces cerevisiae, a species frequently associated with human-managed environments, and its predominantly wild relative S. paradoxus. A genomic survey reveals unexpectedly high hybrid frequencies in geographically distant regions with contrasting environments. Targeted sampling of distilleries and surrounding natural sites reveals a strong ecological bias, with hybrids recovered almost exclusively from distilleries, although both parental species occur in anthropogenic and natural habitats.
items.author: Avelar-Rivas, J. A., Aguirre-Dugua, X., Lopez-Gallegos, C. et al.

items.title: Global homeostatic forces shape the composition of a hyperdiverse tropical insect fauna
items.summary: Despite comprising the bulk of terrestrial biodiversity, we know surprisingly little about insect faunas, particularly in the tropics. Here, we characterize the insect fauna of Madagascar, a global biodiversity hotspot, based on extensive DNA metabarcoding of Malaise trap and leaf litter samples. We estimate that the fauna comprises at least 250,000 species, only 5% of which are currently recorded. The ecological and taxonomic composition is surprisingly similar to that of temperate forests. We show that this is likely caused by global homeostatic forces shaping net diversification rates after colonization of Madagascar rather than by the composition of colonizing lineages. Features differing from temperate forests include the dearth of parasitoids and richness of beetles.
items.author: Ronquist, F., Iwaszkiewicz-Eggebrecht, E., van Dijk, L. J. A. et al.

items.title: Do divergent mitochondrial backgrounds alter the fate of nuclear alleles during hybridization and admixture?
items.summary: Hybridization brings together genetic variation from different populations or species into admixed genomes. As selection sorts this variation, the fate of each allele is determined by its fitness effect in the new hybrid genomic background. Because mitochondrial genes coevolve with the nuclear genome, they may be especially sensitive to foreign nuclear backgrounds, making them potential "hot-spots" for hybrid incompatibilities. Here, we test whether selection against mitonuclear incompatibilities drives repeatable hybridization outcomes. Specifically, we experimentally evolved three sets of five populations of hybrid Drosophila melanogaster, each carrying the same nuclear chromosomes but paired with one of three increasingly divergent mitochondrial DNA backgrounds.
items.author: Darwin, L. J., Bachtel, R. Z., Lemieux, F. A. et al.

items.title: Measuring satellite arrays of the human Y chromosome from sequencing reads
items.summary: Human Y chromosome satellites vary widely but remain difficult to measure in large cohorts. In response, we developed Yruler, which uses pangenome assemblies to measure satellite lengths, composition and Y dosage from sequencing reads without alignment. Analyses reveal centromere-length differences between related lineages, extend observations of short non-centromeric arrays across a lineage, and show unequal component variability and composition changes with heterochromatin length within lineages. Yruler brings satellite variation into population-scale phenotype studies.
items.author: Ortigas-Vasquez, A., Guarracino, A.

items.title: Epigenome-informed Polymer Modeling Reveals Chromosome Folding Landscapes across Distinct Genetic and Epigenetic Contexts
items.summary: Three-dimensional (3D) genome organization is critical for gene regulation, enabling long-range interactions between genes and distal regulatory elements. Genomic structural variations and epigenetic differences can perturb this organization, contributing to phenotypic variation and tissue-specific gene regulation. Prior studies have assessed the impact of these genetic and epigenetic changes on 3D genome folding, primarily using population-averaged features such as topologically associating domains and loops. However, growing evidence from single-cell and live-imaging studies indicates that chromosomes are highly dynamic and exist as heterogeneous ensembles of conformations. Here, we applied an epigenetic-state-informed polymer modeling framework to generate chromosomal conformational ensembles directly from cell- and tissue-specific epigenomic data.
items.author: Bazmi, S., Turco, A., Kumar, S.

items.title: Sexing carnivores from faecal metagenomes: calibrating Rx for stone marten and red fox
items.summary: Knowing the sex of the animal that deposited a scat adds value to non-invasive monitoring, but read-ratio sexing methods were developed for human ancient DNA. We examined their use in shotgun metagenomes of seven stone marten (Martes foina) and red fox (Vulpes vulpes) scats. Human DNA, present in every library, was removed by competitive mapping against the host assembly and the human reference. Applying the Skoglund Ry metric to the marten samples yielded 0 to 25 Y-mapping reads per sample and failed to identify either of the two animals that Rx places firmly in the male range, so we adopted the X-to-autosome ratio Rx of Mittnik et al.

items.title: Provable circuit-level thresholds for non-abelian topological phases
items.summary: We provide an explicit scheme to realize a quantum memory in any 2D non-chiral topological order. For this, we construct syndrome extraction circuits based on the Turaev-Viro path integral as well as a classical algorithm for decoding on the fly. We prove that our scheme has a threshold under a local stochastic circuit-level noise model and discuss how to generalize it to implement topological logical gates.
items.author: Yuanjie Ren, Margarita Davydova, Shankar Balasubramanian et al.

items.title: Joint analysis of the Macquart relation and the dispersion measure power spectrum: cross-covariance and redshift self-calibration
items.summary: The dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs) trace ionised baryons along the line of sight, probing baryonic feedback. Two complementary observables can be constructed from an FRB catalogue: the DM-redshift (Macquart) relation of host-identified FRBs, and the angular power spectrum of the DM field of the full catalogue. Their joint analysis requires their cross-covariance. We derive it within the halo model and show it is a super-sample effect: only the monopole of an individual DM correlates with the angular power spectrum, yielding an exact, model-independent bound on the correlation coefficient. We validate the calculation against log-normal forward simulations of $10^4$ FRBs.
items.author: Amy Wayland, Robert Reischke

items.title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
items.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision. This survey reviews these approaches using two complementary classification axes: teacher-student configuration and the role of quantum resources in the distillation process. Quantum-inspired methods are discussed separately from methods that simulate quantum computations classically or execute them on quantum hardware. We explain how measurement probabilities, expectation values, classical readouts, state overlaps, and circuit-level objectives support different transfer mechanisms. We then critically assess the presented results against baseline design, execution conditions, uncertainty, and resource costs.
items.author: Aldana Al-Sulaiti, Kuan-Cheng Chen, Muhammad Bilal Akram Dastagir et al.

items.title: Room-Temperature Quantum Emission from Boron Nitride Nanotubes
items.summary: Quantum information systems such as quantum key distribution and quantum communications require bright, high-purity, stable sources of single photons to act as carriers of quantum information. As such, methods for obtaining single photon emitters (SPEs) in solid-state devices capable of articulating with quantum photonic circuits are a necessary obstacle that must be overcome. Hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) flakes have been extensively studied as a host material for SPEs, though working in two dimensions is accompanied by engineering complexity. However, dimensionality can be reduced through the implementation of boron nitride nanotubes (BNNTs). Here we investigate the potential of BNNTs as room-temperature SPEs using confocal photoluminescence microscopy and Hanbury Brown-Twiss interferometry.
items.author: Ke-Sean J. M. Peter, Ryan A. Kowalski, David A. Curie et al.

items.title: Testing the Spin of New Physics with Top Precision Measurements
items.summary: Precision measurements can reveal not only the presence of new physics, but also information about the dynamics that generated it. We study this question in top-pair production by comparing three top-philic scenarios: a colored scalar top partner, a colored vector-like fermion, and a spin-one $Z^\prime$ mediator. The first two contribute through loop corrections, while the $Z^\prime$ contributes at tree level. We show that the scalar and vector-like fermion scenarios match onto the same effective operator structure at low energies,making their distinction unfeasible using the EFT approach. However, near or above threshold their full loop amplitudes develop distinct momentum-dependent interference patterns.
items.author: André Lessa, Vinícius Rocca, Veronica Sanz

items.title: Dynamical effects induced by synthetic SU(1,1) gauge fields
items.summary: Compact gauge fields are powerful tools for controlling quantum dynamics and topological phases of matter. Non-compact gauge fields are particularly relevant for open systems, where particles or energy are exchanged with the environment. Here, we investigate the wavepacket and entanglement dynamics induced by an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field. The wavepacket undergoes non-Abelian non-compact Bloch oscillations, in which the spectrum of an auxiliary one-dimensional quantum problem determines the transition between stable oscillations and unstable amplification. In the unstable adiabatic regime, the wavepacket probes an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ topological defect, and its amplification is determined solely by a hyperbolic solid angle in Minkowski space. Threading an $\mathrm{SU}(1,1)$ gauge field through a bosonic tight-binding model yields the bosonic Kitaev model, whose volume or super-volume entanglement scaling is governed by the stability of the gauge field.
items.author: Chenwei Lv

items.title: Polynomial-time classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss
items.summary: Sampling experiments are a leading approach to demonstrating quantum computational advantage, yet their robustness to experimental noise is not completely understood. We develop a common framework for classical simulation of boson and fermion sampling under thermal loss, including pure loss. For Fock-state boson sampling, Gaussian boson sampling with fixed uniform squeezing, and fermion sampling with magic inputs, we obtain polynomial-time sampling at inverse-polynomial total variation error, for any fixed nonzero overall loss rate, and with high probability over Haar-random interferometers. A milder flatness assumption on the ideal output distribution suffices for quasipolynomial-time simulation without Haar randomness. With constant thermal loss per layer, the same flatness assumption gives polynomial-time simulation at logarithmic depth.
items.author: Armando Angrisani, Hela Mhiri

items.title: DiffSequence-Q: Diffusion Design with Quantum Assistance for Biologically Active Proteins
items.summary: Designing protein sequences that satisfy both secondary structure requirements and solubility targets remains challenging. We present DiffSequence-Q, a hybrid multinomial diffusion model conditioned on secondary structure at each residue and a continuous solubility target. To introduce quantum auxiliary supervision during training, we employ a quantum neural network (QNN) or quantum Kolmogorov-Arnold network (QKAN) as an auxiliary solubility prediction head over shared Transformer representations. The auxiliary prediction loss is jointly optimized with the diffusion objective, allowing quantum auxiliary supervision to influence the learned denoising model. Once trained, protein sequences are generated entirely through classical reverse diffusion. On the CATH benchmark, DiffSequence-Q achieved the highest secondary structure recovery among the four evaluated models for complete sequence generation.
items.author: Ke-Xin Tang, Zhen-Qiang Weng, Kai Yan et al.

items.title: Study on hydration cementation and enhancement mechanism of grout-rock interface of PVA modified grouting material
items.summary: by Youwei Li, Haoyu Hu, Yujun Zhang, Gui Liu The weakly cemented sandstone aquifer in coal mine is prone to particle softening under mining disturbance and water-rock interaction, which induces the decrease of rock integrity and the development of water conducting channel, leading to the instability and failure of aquifer. To address the low early-age hydration activity of grouts containing a high proportion of coal gangue, discontinuous grout-rock interfacial bonding, and limited adaptability to weakly cemented sandstone, this paper uses cement and coal gangue(CG) as raw materials to prepare modified grouting materials with different polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) content. The uniaxial compression, XRD, FTIR and SEM test methods were used to systematically study the influence of PVA content on the performance of solid waste based slurry, the bearing characteristics of slurry-rock composite, the evolution of hydration products and the interface micro structure.

items.title: Crafting of physical exhibits by undergraduate medical students: A mixed method study to assess the acquisition of higher-order cognitive skills and student perceptions
items.summary: by Rajesh Kathrotia, Swapnil Paralikar, Vinay Chitturi, Pradip Barde, Gaurav Sharma, Naresh Parmar, Vivek Kumar Sharma, Chinmay Shah Active learning engages students in some activity that induces them to reflect upon ideas and how they are using these ideas. It also involves the process of keeping students mentally, and often physically, active in their learning through activities that engage them in gathering information, thinking, and solving problems. This study was conducted to determine if creating physical exhibits fosters higher-order cognitive skills like problem solving and critical thinking (application and analysis, respectively). items.title: The surgical outcome among children with congenital pseudoarthrosis of Tibia: Our 12 years of experience
items.summary: by Tarun RajBhandari, Sabin Pokharel, Yam Prakash Gurung, Rajan Bhusal, Bibek Banskota, Ashok Kumar Banskota Background Congenital Pseudoarthrosis of the Tibia (CPT) is a rare condition characterized by poorly perfused, invasive hamartomatous fibrous tissue that leads to fracture and pseudoarthrosis of the tibia. Management challenges include achieving union and preventing refractures. This study aims to evaluate surgical interventions and their outcomes in managing congenital pseudoarthrosis of the tibia in children. Materials and methods This retrospective study reviewed 70 CPT cases treated between 2010 and 2022 at Nepal’s only specialized center for children with physical disabilities. It assessed demographics, surgical procedures, and outcomes, with techniques including periosteal grafting and the Masquelet method.
items.author: Tarun RajBhandari, Sabin Pokharel, Yam Prakash Gurung et al.

items.title: An explainable machine learning framework for cross-dataset chronic kidney disease risk prediction using hybrid data balancing
items.summary: by Jarin Tasnim Mumu, Ismail Hossain, Kazi Md. Tanvir Anzum Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a major global health problem, and early detection is important for reducing complications and improving treatment. Machine learning has shown strong potential for CKD prediction, but many existing studies rely on single datasets, face severe class imbalance, and provide limited interpretability. These challenges reduce model reliability and make cross-dataset use in real clinical settings more difficult. Therefore, this study aimed to develop an interpretable and adaptable machine learning framework for CKD risk prediction across different datasets. The proposed hybrid explainable machine learning (HXAI-ML) framework used two public CKD datasets: the UCI CKD Risk Factor Prediction dataset as the source dataset and the Kaggle CKD dataset as the target dataset.
items.author: Jarin Tasnim Mumu, Ismail Hossain, Kazi Md. Tanvir Anzum

items.title: Harpagide alleviates neuroinflammation and cognitive dysfunction in sepsis-associated encephalopathy: Association with the MMP9/NF-κB signaling pathway
items.summary: by Fen Lou, Guochun Deng, Jiejuan Chen, Yijiang Jing, Ao Wang, Mazhong Zhang, Yongping Zhang, Bin Wang Background Sepsis-associated encephalopathy (SAE) is a severe neurological complication of sepsis, characterized by uncontrolled neuroinflammation and cognitive decline, yet no specific therapy is currently available. Harpagide, a naturally occurring iridoid glycoside, has been reported to possess anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective activities; however, its therapeutic potential in SAE remains unexplored. This study aimed to investigate whether Harpagide exerts neuroprotective effects in SAE and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. Methods A mouse model of SAE was established by intraperitoneal injection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS, 18 mg/kg).
items.author: Fen Lou, Guochun Deng, Jiejuan Chen et al.

items.title: Unveiling Molecular Basis of Terminalia chebula in Modulating the AGE-RAGE-PRKCB Axis in Diabetic Nephropathy: Integrative Network Pharmacology and Computational Study
items.summary: by S. M. Riaduzzaman Niaz, Sumaia Jannat, Sheikh Abdullah Al Ashik, Md. Khairul Islam AbstractDiabetic nephropathy (DN), a progressive microvascular complication of diabetes, remains a principal cause of renal failure worldwide, yet its multifaceted molecular complexity continues to challenge effective therapeutic intervention. In this study, an integrative network pharmacology and computational modeling framework was employed to unravel the mechanistic basis of Terminalia chebula in mitigating DN pathology. A total of 357 phytoconstituents were retrieved from the IMPPAT 2.0 and PubChem databases and screened through SwissADME and pkCSM, yielding 14 bioactive, drug-like, and non-toxic compounds. Target prediction integrated data from SwissTargetPrediction, BindingDB, and CTD, while DN-related genes were compiled from GeneCards, OMIM, and transcriptomic datasets (GSE154561, GSE154881, GSE217709, and GSE30528).
items.author: S. M. Riaduzzaman Niaz, Sumaia Jannat, Sheikh Abdullah Al Ashik et al.

items.title: Potential antimicrobial activity, antioxidant, and anti-wrinkle effects of Linum usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel
items.summary: by Ahmad M. Eid, Mohammed Hawash, Linda Issa, Areej Joma, Ansam Joma, Deema Tumeh Background Linum usitatissimum ( L. usitatissimum ) seeds have been reported to have several biological efficacies, such as antioxidant, anti-aging, sun protection, and antimicrobial actions. The present study aimed to develop L. usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel and evaluate its cosmeceutical and antimicrobial characteristics for use in topical applications. Method L. usitatissimum oil nanoemulgel formulations were prepared by optimizing the non-ionic surfactant (Tween® 20, Tween® 80, and Span® 80) using a self-nanoemulsifying technique, followed by the addition of Carbopol®. The droplet size, polydispersity index, zeta potential, and rheological behavior of the emulgel formulations were measured.
items.author: Ahmad M. Eid, Mohammed Hawash, Linda Issa et al.

items.title: The impact of robot-assisted frameless brain biopsy on performance differences between junior and senior neurosurgeons
items.summary: by Carolin Albrecht, Tobias Mahler, Viktor M. Eisenkolb, Benedikt Wiestler, Claire Delbridge, Chiara Negwer, Bernhard Meyer, Arthur Wagner Objective Frameless stereotactic brain biopsy is a standardized and routinely performed neurosurgical procedure, frequently carried out by residents under supervision in academic centers. Robot-assisted (RA) guidance has been introduced to standardize workflow and reduce operator-dependent variability. This study investigates whether RA frameless biopsy reduces experience-related performance differences between residents and attending neurosurgeons compared with a manually operated frameless system (MFS). Methods We performed a retrospective, non-randomized cohort study of consecutive patients undergoing RA frameless stereotactic brain biopsy for intracranial lesions at a tertiary academic center between 2021 and 2025.
items.author: Carolin Albrecht, Tobias Mahler, Viktor M. Eisenkolb et al.

items.title: PIP5K isoforms and phosphoinositide molecular species in EGF-stimulated PIP 3 synthesis: A multi-method approach using enzyme genetic suppression and chemical inhibition in MCF10A cells
items.summary: by Iosif Alexandrou, Vikki Flemington, Martin E. Swarbrick, Sabina Cosulich, Phillip T. Hawkins, Len R. Stephens The membrane phospholipid PI(4,5)P 2 has structural functions and is a substrate for PLC and PI3K enzymes to generate Ins(1,4,5)P 3 , DAG and PI(3,4,5)P 3 signals. PIP5Ks, that 5-phosphorylate PI4P, are the major source of PI(4,5)P 2 in mammalian cells. Current thinking suggests distinct pools of PI(4,5)P 2 may be differentially generated by PIP5Kα, β and γ isoforms and involved in different physiological functions. Phosphoinositides are comprised of families of acyl-chain variants but are uniquely enriched in C38:4 species. There is evidence that PIP5Ks are selective for certain acyl chain species of PI(4)P.
items.author: Iosif Alexandrou, Vikki Flemington, Martin E. Swarbrick et al.

items.title: Gender differences in pre-surgical motivations, expectations, and patient-reported outcomes in Class III orthognathic surgery patients: An item-level analysis
items.summary: by Gizem Altundal, Asuman Deniz Gümrü Celikel, Gülnaz Marsan Objective To evaluate gender differences in pre-surgical motivations, expectations, functional and psychosocial evaluations, and treatment process perceptions among adult patients with skeletal Class III malocclusion undergoing orthodontic preparation for orthognathic surgery. Methods In this single-center, cross-sectional study, 81 adults (37 females, 44 males) with skeletal Class III malocclusion completed a 27-item investigator-developed questionnaire during pre-surgical orthodontic preparation, covering demographics, problem awareness, functional and psychosocial evaluations, motivation and expectations, treatment process, and patient engagement. Gender differences were analyzed item by item with Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, or Fisher’s exact tests. P-values for the 37 comparisons were adjusted with the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) procedure within questionnaire domains, and effect sizes with 95% confidence intervals were estimated.
items.author: Gizem Altundal, Asuman Deniz Gümrü Celikel, Gülnaz Marsan

items.title: Ecological traits predict extinction risk of the world’s traded carnivores
items.summary: by Erik Joaquín Torres-Romero, Maximilian L. Allen, Vincent Nijman, Moreno Di Marco, Christopher J. O’Bryan, Vincenzo Penteriani Wildlife trade is a major driver of biodiversity loss, yet how trade interacts with species’ ecological traits and extinction risk remains underexplored. Carnivores warrant special attention because they are disproportionately exploited and vulnerable to extinction compared to other taxa. We analyzed 171,637 international trade records spanning 50 years (1975–2024) for 129 carnivore species listed under the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). We analyzed trade volumes across the globe and then used logistic regression to evaluate associations between ecological traits and extinction risk, as well as family-level differences in extinction risk.
items.author: Erik Joaquín Torres-Romero, Maximilian L. Allen, Vincent Nijman et al.

items.title: Effectiveness of nurse-led hypertension interventions on retention, adherence, and blood pressure control among adults in low- and middle-income countries: A systematic review
items.summary: by Tagese Yakob, Charuai Suwanbamrung, Cua Ngoc Le, Abebe Sorsa Badacho, Udomsak Saengow Background Hypertension affects more than 1.28 billion adults globally and remains the leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease, stroke, renal failure, and premature death. This burden is inconsistently distributed across Low- and Middle-Income Countries (LMICs), where nearly three-quarters of adults live with hypertension. This gap is largely driven by poor adherence and low retention. This systematic review aims to assess the effectiveness of nurse-led interventions on retention in care, medication adherence, and blood pressure among adult patients with hypertension in primary health care settings in LMICs.

Despite the availability of vaccines and therapeutic agents, the emergence of new variants and drug-resistant strains highlights the need for additional antiviral strategies. items.summary: by Lei Fan, Yixin Liang, Zixian Li, Yan Zhou Although temperate monsoon climate regions are traditionally known for their harsh winter climates, the combined effects of rapid urbanization and global climate change have significantly intensified summer urban heat island effects in these areas, making them a neglected yet increasingly severe challenge in high-latitude urban climate adaptation planning. This study takes a typical campus in Shenyang, a temperate monsoon climate region in Northeast China, as the experimental subject. It quantitatively dissects the non-linear statistical associations and regulatory mechanisms of biotic and abiotic landscape elements and their spatial configurations on microclimate parameters and human thermal comfort (Physiologically Equivalent Temperature, PET) by combining microclimate field observations with validated ENVI-met numerical simulations.

items.title: Fabrication and evaluation of a sulfacetamide-loaded niosomal gel for the treatment of ocular bacterial infections
items.summary: by Neda Sistani Karampour, Pouya Dolati, Anayatollah Salim, Maryam Abedini Baghbadorani, Maryam Keykhaee, Somayeh Handali, Eskandar Moghimipour Topical ocular drug delivery is often restricted by rapid precorneal clearance, which can decrease drug residence time and bioavailability at the ocular surface. The purpose of the study was to develop a sulfacetamide-loaded niosomal gel (SA-Nio-Gel) to enhance ocular drug delivery. Thin film hydration method was used for the preparation of SA niosomes, employing nonionic surfactants (Span 60 and Span 80) and cholesterol. The optimized niosomal formulation was then incorporated into a Carbopol 934 gel base to prepare the final SA-Nio-Gel formulation. The optimized niosomes exhibited encapsulation efficiency of 76% ± 1.5 and a mean particle size of 129.7 ± 2.52 nm.

items.title: Ensemble frequency ratio-maximum entropy landslide susceptibility modelling for climate‑resilient road corridors in Bocas del Toro and Chiriquí, Panama

Singh, Enrique Williams, Jeffrey Gerardo Ramos Perez, Rachel Collin Landslides are a major rainfall-triggered hazard affecting road infrastructure across the mountainous terrain of western Panama. This study develops an ensemble Frequency Ratio (FR)-Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) modelling framework to assess landslide susceptibility, identify critical management zones, and determine key drivers of slope failure along road corridors in the mainland districts of Bocas del Toro and along the Rambala-Hornito-David route. Within a 1,000 m corridor buffer, 87 mapped landslides (63 for training and 24 for validation) and 15 environmental conditioning factors were used to develop and validate the FR and MaxEnt models.

We examined its association with dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-derived adiposity using the nationally representative 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES). Methods This cross-sectional study included adults aged ≥40 years reporting usual weekday and weekend bedtimes and wake times. Social jetlag, the absolute difference between weekday and weekend sleep midpoints, was categorized as Results Among 4,483 participants, 267 (6.0%) had social jetlag ≥2 h.

items.title: Land degradation neutrality state and progress in the Central Region, Malawi
items.summary: by Kennedy Sones Nazombe, Charles Bakolo, Brighton A. Chunga, Principal Mdolo, Jean Mtethiwa, Rodrick Mlewa, Kennedy Adamson, Devie Chilonga, Kelvin Chomanika Achieving Land Degradation Neutrality (LDN) is vital for the long-term sustainability of human well-being and the realisation of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 15.3.1. We estimated the overall indicator of SDG 15.3.1, the proportion of land that is degraded over the total land area in the Central Region, Malawi, from 2001 to 2022, using the Trends.Earth tool in QGIS. The study applied the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) Good Practice Guidance methodology for SDG Indicator 15.3.1 assessment, integrating land cover, land productivity, and soil organic carbon (SOC) sub-indicators.

items.title: A lightweight vision-based framework for automated aero-engine blade damage inspection
items.summary: by Xiaobo Ning, Hang Zhao, Kang Zeng, Zhengwei Zhang Automated visual inspection of aero-engine blades is central to aviation safety, yet it is challenged by damage that is small and low-contrast against a strongly textured metal surface, and by the need for models that are light enough for edge deployment. This paper presents a lightweight vision-based framework for automated blade damage inspection. Rather than assembling independent detection modules, the framework is organized as a three-stage inspection pipeline: (1) a multi-scale feature-discrimination stage (MSBlock) captures defects across a wide size range at negligible computational cost; (2) a texture-suppression stage (TSA) filters high-frequency machining-background noise through product-based channel–spatial attention, exposing genuine defects; and (3) an efficient-prediction stage (Detect_Efficient) fuses cross-scale features and recalibrates confidence with roughly half the parameters of a standard head.

items.title: Modeling and controlling a half-car model suspension system using an ANFIS controller
items.summary: by Sisay Ewunetie Fisha, Amanuel Gebisa Aga, Tatek Mamo Wachamo Passive suspension systems (PSS) use fixed spring and damping characteristics and cannot adapt to changing road disturbances and operating conditions. Active suspension systems (ASS) address this limitation by generating additional control forces, but controller design must balance ride comfort, road holding, model uncertainty, and control effort. This study develops a four-degree-of-freedom (4-DOF) longitudinal half-car model and evaluates an Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) controller against PSS and PID-controlled ASS under double-bump and ISO-classified random Type A and Type C Road profiles at 10 and 20 m/s. The ANFIS controller is trained using PID-generated input-output data with two inputs, five Gaussian membership functions per input, 25 Takagi-Sugeno rules, and 150 training epochs.

items.title: Enjoy Life LocallY (ELLY): A qualitative study of a co-designed healthy weight and wellbeing intervention in two disadvantaged Scottish communities
items.summary: by Julie Cowie, Rhonda Archibald, Scott Findlay, Danielle Hutcheon, Sinéad Currie, Louise Hay, Elizabeth Cook People who are unable to achieve a healthy lifestyle are at greater risk of type II diabetes, some cancers, heart disease, stroke, mobility problems and poor outcomes from disease. For individuals living in disadvantaged areas, life circumstances such as low income, unemployment, working anti-social hours and limited local services present barriers to the challenge of living healthy lives. Working with two disadvantaged communities in Forth Valley, Scotland, we co-designed and implemented an evidence-informed, incentive-based intervention, Enjoy Life LocallY (ELLY), to support citizens with healthy weight and wellbeing.

items.title: Perceived importance, self-rated performance satisfaction, learning stress, and practicum experiences among nursing students: A cross-sectional study with supplementary open-ended responses
items.summary: by Hsiu-Wen Tsai, Shu-Ching Chen This cross-sectional study examined nursing students’ perceived importance and self-rated performance satisfaction regarding fundamental nursing practicum competencies, explored learning-stress scores across academic-achievement categories and psychological-counseling history, and descriptively summarized written practicum experiences. All 730 eligible third-year nursing students were invited; 28 did not participate, 702 returned signed consent forms and questionnaires, and 3 incomplete questionnaires were excluded, leaving 699 participants. Importance–performance analysis (IPA) used sample grand means (importance, 4.679; performance satisfaction, 4.503) as crosshairs. Paired importance–performance gaps and 95% confidence intervals were calculated, and 5,000 bootstrap samples assessed coordinate uncertainty and quadrant stability. Exploratory grade-group and counseling-history comparisons used analysis of variance and independent-samples t tests, respectively, with Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction.

items.title: Amplified MS2 labeling reveals heterogeneous dynamics of RNA granules in the live murine brain ex vivo
items.summary: by Hyungsik Lim, Grace P. Cooper Dynamics of messenger ribonucleic acids (mRNAs) and the complexes with associated proteins (RNPs), also known as RNA granules, provide post-transcriptional control of gene expression. This regulation is crucial for cell-type diversity and activity-dependent plasticity of the mammalian central nervous system (CNS). However, elucidating the physiological significance of RNA granules has been hampered by technical difficulties to probe them in live brain. Here, we describe a novel method to visualize RNA granules in native CNS tissues of mouse. To amplify the fluorescence signal from single mRNAs incorporating MS2 stem loops, MS2 capsid protein (MCP) was conjugated with 4 tandem superfolder green fluorescent proteins (sfGFPs).

items.title: Multi-Probe Cosmological Constraints on Clustering DBI Dark Energy Scenario
items.summary: We present a multi-probe observational analysis of a clustering tachyonic Dirac-Born-Infeld~(DBI) dark energy model. Its noncanonical kinetic term gives a subluminal sound speed, so dark energy perturbations can grow on subhorizon scales. Working in a multifluid framework that tracks both the background expansion and linear perturbations, we constrain the model with nested sampling, using Planck 2018 compressed CMB distance priors, DESI DR2 BAO, cosmic chronometers, $fσ_8$ growth data, and three Type Ia supernova compilations: Pantheon$+$, DES-SN5YR, and Union3. The standard cosmological parameters agree with $Λ$CDM within $2σ$, with DBI preferring a slightly lower $H_0$ and higher $Ω_{m0}$, with the largest shift being $\simeq1.8σ$ in $H_0$ for Pantheon$+$.

items.title: Quantum Relative Entropy and Information Flux Resolve Wavefunction Collapse in Spacelike-Separated QED Waveguides
items.summary: Resolving how first-order quantum coherence and definite measurement outcomes emerge from entangled vacuum fluctuations across spacelike-separated regions is unified here by the principle that quantum relative entropy governs the energy-information flux across causal boundaries [P.~Dorau and A.~Much, Phys.~Rev.~Lett.~\textbf{136}, 091602 (2026)]. We establish the exact quantum-optical realization of this principle using dual, spacelike-separated entangled nonlinear biphoton sources implemented in quantum electrodynamics waveguides pumped by an optical frequency comb and seeded by a continuous-wave laser in a coherent state $|α\rangle$. We demonstrate that single-photon-added coherent states (SPACS) generated via coherent seeding possess a quantum relative entropy that precisely quantifies the entanglement deficit between signal and idler fields.

items.title: Crosstalk-Induced Row Hammer Attacks on Quantum Random Access Codes
items.summary: Quantum processors remain susceptible to crosstalk-induced effects despite the continuous evolution of their underlying hardware architectures. In this work, we experimentally investigate the effectiveness of crosstalk-induced attacks across six IBM superconducting quantum processors and one IQM processor. Our results demonstrate that such attacks can be launched across all the platforms, due to persistance of crosstalk, although their effectiveness varies significantly between devices. The probability of a measurement outcome flip in the victim qubits reaches a maximum value of $60\%$. Also, it is seen that processors sharing identical coupling graphs exhibit different vulnerability profiles, indicating that connectivity alone is insufficient to predict attack efficiency.

items.title: Autler-townes energy-level engineering for high-quality all-microwave qubit gate
items.summary: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for realizing large-scale fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computing, yet existing approaches are limited: frequency-tuning techniques induce decoherence, while all-microwave-driven schemes suffer the trade-off between gate speed and leakage rate. Here, we introduce an energy-level engineering technique that employs the Autler-Townes effect to manipulate the nonlinearity of qubits without perturbing the computational subspace or degrading coherence time. This approach enables an experimentally validated, fast (97 ns) and high-fidelity (99.40(9)%) CZ gate, where error analysis reveals that gate errors arise mainly from static decoherence. The scheme facilitates fast, high-quality all-microwave gate operations with a simple topology and can be applied across various quantum platforms.

items.title: Monopoles, Scattering and Generalized Symmetries on a Quantum Computer
items.summary: Quantum computers have advanced to the stage that interesting many-body quantum phenomena can be observed. A striking example is the magnetic monopole paradox, a problem that was only solved recently using the language of generalized symmetries. Here we demonstrate a quantum spin chain analogue of magnetic monopole scattering on Quantinuum System Model H2. We implement a novel protocol for preparing a localized quasiparticle wavepacket on top of the ground state. By combining this protocol with time evolution across a duality defect, we efficiently convert local particles into non-local string-like excitations. We demonstrate this particle-to-string conversion in the transverse-field Ising model and a symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase of the cluster model.

items.title: Can $n_s$ hint at a parity-odd sector of gravity?
items.summary: We study slow-roll inflation in the context of metric-affine gravity. We consider the most general projectively invariant metric-affine theory at most quadratic in the distortion and linear in curvature with no propagating torsion and non-metricity and couple it non-minimally to a scalar field. We focus on the class of $ξ$-attractors, in which a single function $f(φ)$ fixes the whole scalar sector. Integrating out the non-dynamical distortion generates a correction to the kinetic term $k(φ)$ which is $f'(φ)^2$ times a ratio of polynomials in $f(φ)$. The new kinetic term can develop poles at finite field values, where the distortion field equations degenerate.

items.title: Negative non-linear differential dissipation in mechanical quartz resonators
items.summary: We observe negative non-linear differential dissipation in a low-frequency (32.7 kHz) miniature quartz tuning fork, representing a high-Q piezoelectric resonator, at temperatures below 0.3 K. Similar drive-induced dissipation suppression has previously been reported in superconducting microwave resonators, and high-frequency MEMS devices, associated to coupling with tunneling two-level systems (TTLSs). In the case of low-frequency resonators, the equivalent temperature of the mechanical mode is orders of magnitude lower than the thermodynamic temperature of the device, implying that accessible TTLS states are largely saturated. We demonstrate that the observed temperature and drive dependence of the losses fit well within the framework of an interacting TTLS bath, indicating the presence of a channel for energy transfer between the mechanical mode and thermally activated TTLSs.

This is part of the SPOQC mission by Quantum Communications Hub, UK which was successfully launched on March 2026.
